reconciliation_2023.key_observation: Both tables reconcile to their own balance sheet on OUTSTANDING (incurred less paid), so the restatement leaves outstanding untouched and moves incurred and paid by the same amounts. Implied cumulative paid at end-2022 on the 2023 basis = 253,729 - 108,937 = 144,792 vs 83,123 printed in 2022 (diff 61,669 = the incurred diff 253,729 - 192,060 = 61,669). Neither paid nor incurred history in the 2023 table can be tied to the 2022 print.

rollforward_2023.agreement_with_M: M = +42,378 does not agree with a 2023 prior-year line of ~2.9m (closed-year) or 9.26m net (2021-and-prior YOA, p7). It also cannot fit inside total gross incurred: 58,191 less 2022-UY movement (63,498 - 33,254 = 30,244) less 2023 UY first-year (21,300) leaves about 6.6m for UYs 2020-2021 (derived, residual; 7.1m with the 447 FX). The 104m measured from the 2022 diagonal is impossible (it exceeds total gross incurred of 58.2m). Table movements in 2023 sum to 2,881 + 39,497 + 30,244 + 21,300 = 93,922 vs 58,191 gross incurred, a 35.7m excess sitting in the 2020-21 rows; net table movements 4,228 + 42,376 + 30,600 + 18,258 = 95,462 vs net incurred 55,377 (excess 40.1m). By contrast the 2023 UY (net 18,258 vs 18,248 p7) and 2022 UY (net 30,600 vs 27,870 p7) rows tie closely to the calendar-year table, so the excess is in the 2020-21 rows. The 2020 gross row movement (+2,881) does match the printed '$2.9m deterioration on closed year reserves' (p47), which points to 2020 being a true 2023 movement and the 2021 +39,497 (restated base) being the problem row.

2689_2023.true_movement_notes: The filing does not print a gross 2020-21 movement. Indicators: (a) gross 2020 row +2.881m equals the printed '$2.9m deterioration on closed year reserves' (p47); (b) net calendar-year claims incurred on 2021-and-prior YOA 9.26m (p7), which includes current-year exposure; (c) derived residual of total gross incurred 58.191m less 2022-UY row 30.244m less 2023-UY 21.300m = about 6.6m for UYs 2020-21 together. So the true 2023 gross development of 2020-21 is of order 3m to 9m, not 42.4m and not 104m. These are my derivations from printed lines, not a figure the filing states.
2689_2023.note: Both tables carry the same heading and basis wording, both reconcile to their balance-sheet gross claims outstanding, and no restatement note or 2023 transaction exists, so presentation alone is not explained; yet the 2023 table's historical incurred and paid cells for UYs 2020-21 are higher than the 2022 print by amounts that net to zero in outstanding (end-2022 incurred 253,729 vs 192,060; paid implied 144,792 vs 83,123), and the 2023 table's year-on-year movement exceeds the 2023 income statement's total gross incurred by 35.7m. M = +42.378m therefore rests on a rebased history (largely the 2021 column, +39.5m) that is not 2023 development, and using the 2022 diagonal (104m) is worse. Not an RITC/transfer (none in 2023). Possible 'development' reading is not supported by the income statement tie-out. The paid history is also unexplained: the 2023 table's cumulative paid rose 133,076 across 2020-2023 rows vs gross claims paid of 36,123 in 2023, on the 2022 base; so the filings contain an unexplained inconsistency in the earlier years of the table. Recommend excluding or treating as undeterminable-for-M-size if a conservative rule is preferred; my reading is restated_base.
